title: Jowar (Sorghum): modeled ₹493/qtl left, Gadag → Bidar
summary: April 2022: reported jowar (Sorghum) prices at Gadag and Bidar imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 18 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹493 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 6 same-variety market pairs screened for jowar (Sorghum) in April 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Jowar ( White), FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Bidar report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: April 2022
scenes.caption: Gadag (Karnataka) and Bidar (Karnataka) both reported jowar (Sorghum) prices for the same variety and grade (Jowar ( White), FAQ) on 18 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Gadag reported a median ₹1,969 per quintal. Bidar reported a median ₹2,800 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹840/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹840 per quintal, and Bidar was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 418 km by road
scenes.caption: 418 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~6 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹90/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹493 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹329 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Bidar report, the rule selects 18 of 18 modeled shipping days. 18 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹493 per quintal (₹329 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Jowar (Sorghum) route from Gadag to Bidar was positive on 100% of matched days in April 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹49,300, or ₹32,900 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to jowar (Sorghum)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹90/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Jowar (Sorghum) route from Gadag to Bidar was positive on 100% of matched days in April 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹49,300, or ₹32,900 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
